fact: The brightest star of Lyra, and once — and future — Pole Star as Earth's axis slowly precesses.
bio: Vega (Alpha Lyrae) is a nearby hot white star, only 25 light-years away, that long served as the zero-point reference for the astronomical magnitude scale. It rotates so fast it is noticeably flattened.
cultural: Vega was the northern pole star around 12,000 BCE and will be again near 13,700 CE. It anchors the Summer Triangle with Deneb and Altair, and stars in Carl Sagan's Contact as the source of the alien signal.
